_Title: User Interfaces, Video Programming Guides and Menus
_Applicability:
> This rule applies to:

-   Devices that receive or playback video programming (such as the Xbox
    One, Xbox 360, Xbox Blu-ray/DVD player, PCs, Phones and Tablets,
    Surface, and SurfaceHub),

-   Devices that have preinstalled video applications, whether our own
    or third party (such as the Xbox OneGuide, Microsoft Movies & TV,
    Groove, Windows Media Player, and preinstalled third-party
    applications such as Netflix, Hulu, or Amazon), and

-   Video applications that we direct people to use to access video
    programming,

> If those devices have

-   Onscreen menus that offer any of 11 specific video playback
    functions, or

-   Offer video playback functionality in a manner other than onscreen
    text menus, such as a power on/off on hardware.
_Requirement:
Any User Interface (UI) that a person must navigate in order to launch
applications that play video programming must be accompanied by audio
output (such as through a screen reader). The following functions, if
offered through an onscreen text menu, must be accompanied by audible
output:

1.  *Power on / off*

2.  *Volume adjust / mute *

3.  *Channel / program selection (including on-demand programming)*
    Function that allows the user to select channels and programs (e.g.,
    via physical numeric or channel up/channel down buttons or via on
    screen guides and menus)

4.  *Display channel / program information (including on-demand
    programming)*

5.  *Configuration / set-up (for example, language selection, parental
    controls)*  
    Function that allows the user to access and change configuration or
    setup options (e.g., configuration of video display and audio
    settings, selection of preferred language for onscreen guides or
    menus, etc.).

6.  *Enable / disable closed captioning *

7.  *Configuration of closed captioning options (for example, changing
    font size, color) *

8.  *Enable / disable video description *

9.  *Display configuration info  
    *Function that allows the user to display how user preferences are
    currently configured

10. *Playback functions (for example, play, pause, rewind, fast forward,
    stop, and record) *

11. *Input selection* Function that allows the user to select their
    preferred input source.

Covered devices and applications are not required to include any or all
of these functions, but if they are included, they must be accessible.

If any of these 11 functions are offered other than through on-screen
menus"for example, power-on functionality could be activated via the
hardware"then those functions must still be accessible for individuals
without vision, with low vision and limited or no hearing, and with
limited or no color perception.

A feature is "accessible" if the input, control, and mechanical
functions are locatable, identifiable, and operable for a person with a
disability. A person with a disability should have at least one method
for using the feature that provides equivalent functionality as is
available to users without a disability. For example, the power-on
mechanical control should be tactilely discernable to aid use by
individuals with visual impairments; patterns should be used to augment
color cues for those with limited color perception.

Video programming is programming by, or comparable to, programming
provided by a television broadcast station, including when such video
programming is delivered using Internet Protocol (IP). It does not
include user-generated content, unless that content is subsequently
broadcast on television with captions.

_Title: Closed Captioning, Video Description and Emergency Information Activation
_Applicability:
This rule applies to:

-   Devices that receive, play back, or record video programming (such
    as but not limited to the Xbox One, Xbox 360, Xbox Blu-ray/DVD
    player, PCs, Phones and Tablets, and Surface);

-   Devices that have preinstalled video applications, our own or third
    party (such as the Xbox OneGuide, Microsoft Movies & TV, Groove,
    Windows Media Player, or preinstalled third-party applications such
    as Netflix, Hulu, or Amazon); and

-   Players that are preinstalled or that Microsoft directs consumers to
    use in order to access linear programming on our devices (such as
    Xbox TV).
_Requirement:
If your product or service offers closed captioning or video description
functionality, that function must be activated by an easy-to-locate and
simple-to-use mechanism such as a button, key, or icon.

Players that are preinstalled or that Microsoft directs consumers to use
in order to access linear programming on our devices (such as Xbox TV)
and players that record video programming comparable to that provided by
broadcasters must provide a simple and easy to use mechanism (such as a
button, key, or icon) for activating the secondary audio stream for
audible emergency information.

Video programming is programming provided by, or generally considered
comparable to programming provided by, a television broadcast station
(whether distributed over the air, by cable or satellite), but not
including consumer-generated media.

Linear programming is prescheduled (as opposed to on-demand) broadcast
programming delivered via cable, satellite, or over the air.

_Applicability:
This rule applies to devices and video players capable of displaying media content with closed captions. 

Note: See [MAS 7.1.4.1](https://aka.ms/mas7.1.4.1) for devices and video players subject to the CVAA. These include video players (for example, apps and browsers with built-in players), devices with preinstalled video players, and devices that can record or play back video programming. The FCC defines �video programming� as �programming provided by, or generally considered comparable to programming provided by, a television broadcast station, but not including consumer-generated media.� 

This rule does not apply to: 
- applications with built-in players that are only used for video creation or editing
- video communications
_Requirement:
Devices and video players capable of displaying media content with closed captions shall provide a way for users to change caption display characteristics, except where the captions are displayed as unmodifiable characters. 

Notes:
- Defining the background and foreground color of captions, font type, size, opacity of the background box of captions, and the contour or border of the fonts can contribute to meeting this requirement. 
- Captions that are bitmap images are examples of unmodifiable characters. 
- This requirement does not apply to video communications. See the MAS 6.6 series for applicable requirements.
_Guidance: MAS 7.1.4 - Caption characteristics is based on these standards: - EN 301 549: 7.1.4 Captions characteristics (PDF)

_Title: Hearing Aid Compatibility (HAC) for Mobile Handsets - Product Documentation
_Applicability: This rule applies if the mobile handset is manufactured or imported for use in the United States (including US territories) and is used with voice communications. A phablet is considered a mobile handset for this purpose. A tablet or PC that is not typically held to the ear is not considered a mobile handset covered by this rule.
_Requirement:
The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has specific requirements for documenting the hearing aid compatibility of phones on product packages, in product inserts and user manuals, and on websites.

**Product packages, product inserts, and user manuals:** � Package label � The package label for hearing-aid compatible handsets must state that the handset is hearing aid-compatible. If the handset was certified using a technical standard with volume control requirements, the package label must include the handset's actual conversational gain with and without a hearing aid. � Package insert or handset manual � For hearing-aid compatible handsets, the following information must be disclosed to consumers in a package insert or in the handset's user manual:

- A statement that the handset is hearing aid-compatible - The ANSI standard used to determine the hearing aid compatibility of the handset - If the 2011 ANSI standard or an earlier version was used: the lowest hearing aid compatibility rating assigned to any of the covered air interfaces or frequency bands - The air interfaces or frequency bands that are not certified to be hearing aid-compatible, if applicable, or have been determined to be hearing aid-compatible under special testing circumstances - The language below must be included for any handset certified to be hearing aid-compatible for some but not all air interfaces or frequency bands:

�This phone has been tested and certified for use with hearing aids for some of the wireless technologies that it uses. However, there may be some newer wireless technologies used in this phone that have not been tested yet for use with hearing aids. It is important to try the different features of this phone thoroughly and in different locations, using your hearing aid or cochlear implant, to determine if you hear any interfering noise. Consult your service provider or the manufacturer of this phone for information on hearing aid compatibility. If you have questions about return or exchange policies, consult your service provider or phone retailer.�

- An explanation of the ANSI rating system, including an explanation that the 2019 ANSI standard does not use the same rating system as older versions of the standard - If the handset was certified using a technical standard that includes volume control requirements: an explanation of the handset�s volume control capabilities, including its conversational gain both with and without hearing aids - If a handset has air interfaces that have been certified as hearing aid-compatible under special testing circumstances: an explanation of those circumstances and how those circumstances affect the use and operation of the handset

**Websites:**

A list of all hearing aid-compatible models currently offered, the ratings of those models, and an explanation of the rating system must be made available on a website. The information on the website must be updated within 30 days of any relevant changes, and any website pages containing information so updated must indicate the day on which the update occurred.

See [MAS 8.6 � Hearing Aid Compatibility (HAC) for Mobile Handsets (T mode)](https://aka.ms/8.6) and [MAS 8.7 Hearing Aid Compatibility (HAC) for Mobile Handsets (M mode)](https://aka.ms/8.7) for further information on Hearing Aid Compatibility requirements.
_Guidance:
MAS 10.4 - Hearing Aid Compatibility (HAC) for Mobile Handsets � Product Documentation is based on these regulations and guidance documents: - FCC

- 47 CFR �20.19(f)(1) Hearing aid compatibility; labeling requirements

(1) **Package label.** For all handset models certified to be hearing aid-compatible, manufacturers and service providers shall ensure that the handset's package label states that the handset is hearing aid-compatible and the handset's actual conversational gain with and without a hearing aid if certified using a technical standard with volume control requirements. The actual conversational gain displayed for use with a hearing aid shall be the lowest rating assigned to the handset for any covered air interface or frequency band.

(2) **Package insert or handset manual.** For all handset models certified to be hearing aid-compatible, manufacturers and service providers shall disclose to consumers through the use of a package insert or in the handset's user manual:

(i) That the handset is hearing aid-compatible;

(ii) The ANSI standard used to determine the hearing aid compatibility of the handset model's air interfaces and frequency bands;

(iii) If using the 2011 ANSI standard or an earlier version of the standard, the lowest hearing aid compatibility rating assigned to any of the covered air interfaces or frequency bands;

(iv) The air interfaces or frequency bands on the handset that are not certified to be hearing aid-compatible, if applicable, or have been determined to be hearing aid-compatible under special testing circumstances;

(v) Any handset model certified to be hearing aid-compatible for some but not all of the air interfaces or frequency bands covered by the model must include the following disclosure language:

This phone has been tested and certified for use with hearing aids for some of the wireless technologies that it uses. However, there may be some newer wireless technologies used in this phone that have not been tested yet for use with hearing aids. It is important to try the different features of this phone thoroughly and in different locations, using your hearing aid or cochlear implant, to determine if you hear any interfering noise. Consult your service provider or the manufacturer of this phone for information on hearing aid compatibility. If you have questions about return or exchange policies, consult your service provider or phone retailer.

(vi) An explanation of the ANSI rating system, which includes an explanation that the 2019 ANSI standard does not use the rating system that older versions of the standard used;

(vii) An explanation of a handset model's volume control capabilities, including its conversational gain both with and without hearing aids, if the handset is certified using a technical standard that includes volume control requirements; and

(viii) An explanation of special testing circumstances, if a handset model has air interfaces that have been certified as hearing aid-compatible under such circumstances, and how these circumstances affect the use and operation of the handset.

- 47 CFR �20.19(h) Hearing aid compatibility; website and record retention requirements

(1) Each manufacturer and service provider that operates a publicly-accessible website must make available on its website a list of all hearing aid-compatible models currently offered, the ratings of those models, and an explanation of the rating system.

(4) The information on the website must be updated within 30 days of any relevant changes, and any website pages containing information so updated must indicate the day on which the update occurred.

_Applicability:
This rule applies to authoring tools. An authoring tool is *any software that can be used by authors, alone or collaboratively, to create or modify content or to develop applications or services, for use by other people (other authors or end users).*

Notes:
- �Content� includes documents, websites, blogs, images, video, and user-generated content. 
- Any software that offers an ability for authors or end users to create rich text content is considered an authoring tool. 
- Any software that **only** offers an ability for authors or end users to create plain text content is **not** considered an authoring tool.
_Requirement:
Authoring tools must prompt users to create or edit applications, services, tools, and content that is accessible.  

Notes: 

A prompt is any?authoring tool-initiated request for a decision or piece of information from?authors. The term covers both requests that must be responded to immediately (e.g., modal dialog boxes) as well as less urgent requests (e.g., underlining a misspelled word). Authoring tools containing accessibility checkers satisfy this requirement, as does providing the ability for users to add alt-text to images.

_Requirement:
**As of June 28, 2025**, products subject to the European Accessibility Act (EAA) must meet the following packaging and labeling requirements: � Information provided on the product itself (e.g., labelling, instructions, warnings) must be written in a clear, understandable manner and be accessible. - **Note:** One way the accessibility aspect of this requirement might be met is to provide an accessible QR code on the product that takes the user to an accessible website that contains product information. If a QR code is provided, it must be accompanied by a printed URL for individuals that are unable to scan a QR code. � Instructions for the installation, maintenance, storage, and disposal of the product that are not provided on the product itself, and are provided through other means, such as a website, must be written in a clear, understandable manner and meet all applicable MAS requirements. � Packaging - Packaging and any information provided in the packaging must be accessible. - **Note:** One way this requirement might be met is to provide an accessible QR code on the packaging that takes the user to an accessible website that contains the information displayed on or provided in the packaging. If a QR code is provided, it must be accompanied by a printed URL for individuals that are unable to scan a QR code. - Information provided on the package must be accessible, if feasible.

The following products are covered by the EAA: � general purpose computer hardware systems intended for consumer use (for example, personal computers, including desktops, notebooks, smartphones, and tablets) � operating systems for general purpose computer hardware systems intended for consumer use, including OS pre-installed on a device and OS sold as standalone software � consumer devices primarily used to access electronic communication services (for example, phones, routers, and modems) � consumer devices whose main purpose is accessing audiovisual media services (for example, set-top boxes and television sets) � e-readers

_Title: Information for Consumers � Computer Hardware and Operating Systems
_Applicability:
This rule applies to the following products: - general purpose computer hardware systems intended for consumer use (for example, personal computers, including desktops, notebooks, smartphones and tablets) - operating systems for those computers (for example, Windows)

This rule does not apply to: - specialized computers embedded in consumer electronics products (for example, gaming consoles) and operating systems for those products - computer hardware systems intended for enterprise use (for example, HoloLens) and operating systems for those computers - accessories
_Requirement:
General purpose computer hardware systems intended for consumer use (for example, personal computers, including desktops, notebooks, smartphones, and tablets) and operating systems for those computers (for example, Windows) must be accompanied by instructions for the use of the product. The instructions must be accessible and be provided either (a) on the product itself, (b) through the use of the product, or (c) on a website. 

Content meeting applicable MAS will be considered accessible and satisfy this requirement. 

The instructions must include descriptions of the following: 
- the product�s accessibility features and how to operate them 
- the product�s interoperability with assistive technologies, including a list of the assistive technologies tested with the product 
- the product�s user interface, including the features and functionality addressing the following requirements: 
	- if the product provides communication, including interpersonal communication, operation, information, control and orientation, providing it via more than one sensory channel; including providing alternatives to vision, auditory, speech and tactile elements 
	- if the product uses color to convey information, indicate an action, require a response or identify elements, providing an alternative to color 
	- if the product uses audible signals to convey information, indicate an action, require a response or identify elements, providing an alternative to audible signals 
	- if the product uses visual elements, providing flexible ways of improving vision clarity 
	- if the product uses audio, providing user control of volume and speed, and enhanced audio features including the reduction of interfering audio signals from surrounding products and audio clarity 
	- if the product requires manual operation and control, providing for sequential control and alternatives to fine motor control, avoiding the need for simultaneous controls for manipulation, and using tactile discernible parts 
	- avoiding modes of operation requiring extensive reach and great strength 
	- avoiding triggering photosensitive seizures 
	- protecting the user�s privacy when they use accessibility features 
	- providing an alternative to biometrics identification and control 
	- ensuring consistency of functionality and providing enough, and flexible amounts of, time for interaction 
	- providing software and hardware for interfacing with assistive technologies

- European Accessibility Act

**Annex I, Section I**
General accessibility requirements related to all products covered by this Directive in accordance with Article 2(1):

Products must be designed and produced in such a way as to maximise their foreseeable use by persons with disabilities and shall be accompanied where possible in or on the product by accessible information on their functioning and on their accessibility features.
1. Requirements on the provision of information:
b) the instructions for use of a product, where not provided on the product itself but made available through the use of the product or through other means such as a website, including the accessibility functions of the product, how to activate them and their interoperability with assistive solutions shall be publicly available when the product is placed on the market and shall:
(i) be made available via more than one sensory channel;
(ii) be presented in an understandable way;
(iii) be presented to users in ways they can perceive;
(iv) be presented in fonts of adequate size and suitable shape, taking into account foreseeable conditions of use and using sufficient contrast, as well as adjustable spacing between letters, lines and paragraphs;
(v) with regard to content, be made available in text formats that can be used for generating alternative assistive formats to be presented in different ways and via more than one sensory channel;
(vi) be accompanied by an alternative presentation of any non-textual content;
(vii) include a description of the user interface of the product (handling, control and feedback, input and output) which is provided in accordance with point 2; the description shall indicate for each of the points in point 2 whether the product provides those features;
(viii) include a description of the functionality of the product which is provided by functions aiming to address the needs of persons with disabilities in accordance with point 2; the description shall indicate for each of the points in point 2 whether the product provides those features;
(ix) include a description of the software and hardware interfacing of the product with assistive devices; the description shall include a list of those assistive devices which have been tested together with the product.

2. User interface and functionality design:
The product, including its user interface, shall contain features, elements and functions, that allow persons with disabilities to access, perceive, operate, understand and control the product by ensuring that: (a) when the product provides for communication, including interpersonal communication, operation, information, control and orientation, it shall do so via more than one sensory channel; this shall include providing alternatives to vision, auditory, speech and tactile elements;
(b) when the product uses speech it shall provide alternatives to speech and vocal input for communication, operation control and orientation;
c) when the product uses visual elements it shall provide for flexible magnification, brightness and contrast for communication, information and operation, as well as ensure interoperability with programmes and assistive devices to navigate the interface;
(d) when the product uses colour to convey information, indicate an action, require a response or identify elements, it shall provide an alternative to colour;
(e) when the product uses audible signals to convey information, indicate an action, require a response or identify elements, it shall provide an alternative to audible signals;
(f) when the product uses visual elements it shall provide for flexible ways of improving vision clarity;
(g) when the product uses audio it shall provide for user control of volume and speed, and enhanced audio features including the reduction of interfering audio signals from surrounding products and audio clarity;
(h) when the product requires manual operation and control, it shall provide for sequential control and alternatives to fine motor control, avoiding the need for simultaneous controls for manipulation, and shall use tactile discernible parts;
(i) the product shall avoid modes of operation requiring extensive reach and great strength;
(j) the product shall avoid triggering photosensitive seizures;
(k) the product shall protect the user�s privacy when he or she uses the accessibility features;
(l) the product shall provide an alternative to biometrics identification and control;
(m) the product shall ensure the consistency of the functionality and shall provide enough, and flexible amounts of, time for interaction;
(n) the product shall provide software and hardware for interfacing with the assistive technologies.

_Title: Information for Consumers � Electronic Communication Services
_Applicability:
This rule applies to electronic communications services (interpersonal communications services) offered in the European Union that are subject to the European Accessibility Act.

Note: Services that are covered as electronic communications services (interpersonal communications services) under the European Electronic Communications Code (EECC) are subject to the European Accessibility Act.
_Requirement:
Information must be provided to consumers that describes how electronic communication services (internet access services and interpersonal communications services) offered in the European Union meet the requirements of the European Accessibility Act.

The information must be accessible. Content meeting applicable MAS will be considered accessible and satisfy this requirement.

The information must include:
- A general description of the service
	- A description of the service must be entered in the �product description� field in the Accessibility Assessment Tool (AAT) to meet this requirement.
- Instructions for how to use the service
	- The instructions can be provided on a website or within the service itself (for example, Help content). The location of the instructions must be recorded in the �internal notes� field in the AAT. If the instructions are published on a website, enter the url.
- Description of how the service meets the relevant accessibility requirements of EN 301 549.
	- An Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR) must be completed in the AAT to meet this requirement.
- Where first-party devices are designed specifically to provide the service (for example, a mobile phone configured to access a particular mobile operator�s network), a description of how to use the service with the devices as well as information about the devices� accessibility characteristics and interoperability with assistive technology
	- Note: Microsoft does not currently offer devices that fall into this category.

- European Accessibility Act

**Annex I, Section III**

General accessibility requirements related to all services covered by this Directive in accordance with Article 2(2): The provision of services in order to maximise their foreseeable use by persons with disabilities, shall be achieved by: (a) ensuring the accessibility of the products used in the provision of the service, in accordance with Section I of this Annex and, where applicable, Section II thereof;
(b) providing information about the functioning of the service, and where products are used in the provision of the service, its link to these products as well as information about their accessibility characteristics and interoperability with assistive devices and facilities:
(i) making the information available via more than one sensory channel;
(ii) presenting the information in an understandable way;
(iii) presenting the information to users in ways they can perceive;
(iv) making the information content available in text formats that can be used to generate alternative assistive formats to be presented in different ways by the users and via more than one sensory channel;
(v) presenting in fonts of adequate size and suitable shape, taking into account foreseeable conditions of use and using sufficient contrast, as well as adjustable spacing between letters, lines and paragraphs;
(vi) supplementing any non-textual content with an alternative presentation of that content; and
(vii) providing electronic information needed in the provision of the service in a consistent and adequate way by making it perceivable, operable, understandable and robust;

**Annex I, Section IV**

Additional accessibility requirements related to specific services:
The provision of services in order to maximise their foreseeable use by persons with disabilities, shall be achieved by including functions, practices, policies and procedures and alterations in the operation of the service targeted to address the needs of persons with disabilities and ensure interoperability with assistive technologies:
(a) Electronic communications services, including emergency communications referred to in Article 109(2) of Directive (EU) 2018/1972:
(i) providing real time text in addition to voice communication;
(ii) providing total conversation where video is provided in addition to voice communication;

**Article 7**

**Annex IV**

Conformity Assessment Procedure � Products

1. Internal production control
Internal production control is the conformity assessment procedure whereby the manufacturer fulfils the obligations laid down in points 2, 3 and 4 of this Annex, and ensures and declares on its sole responsibility that the product concerned satisfy the appropriate requirements of this Directive.

The manufacturer shall establish the technical documentation. The technical documentation shall make it possible to assess the conformity of the product to the relevant accessibility requirements referred to in Article 4 and, in case the manufacturer relied on Article 14, to demonstrate that relevant accessibility requirements would introduce a fundamental alteration or impose a disproportionate burden. Enable users to connect with third-party captioning services so that captions provided by such services appear on the user�s video conference screen. � Note: Connection to third-party captioning services may be achieved by providing an API. � Note: Microsoft is not responsible for ensuring that third-party captions are accurate and synchronous. However, Microsoft products and services must not impair or impede the delivery of third-party captions.

Provide user interface controls that enable users to activate and adjust the display of captions, including: � changing the size, font, and on-screen location of captions � adjusting the color and opacity of both the captions and the caption background.

_Title: User Controls for Caption Characteristics (CVAA Devices and Players)
_Applicability:
This rule applies to - Devices capable of displaying video programming, such as laptops, smartphones, and gaming consoles, and - First-party video players that Microsoft preinstalls on a device or requires end-users to install on a device.

The FCC defines �video programming� as �programming provided by, or generally considered comparable to programming provided by, a television broadcast station, but not including consumer-generated media.� This rule does not apply to - Third-party video players - Applications with built-in players that are only used for video creation or editing.
_Requirement:
Devices capable of playing video programming and first-party video players that Microsoft either preinstalls on those devices or requires end users to install on those devices must support the specific technical features for closed captions described below: **(1) Presentation.** Captioning shall be implemented such that the caption text may be displayed within one or separate caption windows and supporting the following modes: - a. text that appears a- ll at once (pop-on) - b. text that scrolls up as new text appears (roll-up) and, - c. text where each new letter or word is displayed as it arrives (paint-on).

**(2) Character color.** Captioning shall be implemented such that characters may be displayed in the 64 colors defined in CEA-708 and such that users are provided with the ability to override the authored color for characters and select from a palette of at least 8 colors including: white, black, red, green, blue, yellow, magenta, and cyan. **(3) Character opacity.** Captioning shall be implemented such that users are provided with the ability to vary the opacity of captioned text and select between opaque and semi-transparent opacities. **(4) Character size.** Captioning shall be implemented such that users are provided with the ability to vary the size of captioned text and shall provide a range of such sizes from 50% of the default character size to 200% of the default character size. **(5) Fonts.** - a. Captioning shall be implemented such that fonts are available to implement the eight fonts required by CEA-708 and listed below. Users must be provided with the ability to assign the fonts included on their apparatus as the default font for each of the eight styles. - b. Decoders must support the eight fonts listed below. Caption providers may specify 1 of these 8 font styles to be used to write caption text. The styles specified in the �font style� parameter of the SetPenAttributes command are numbered from 0 through 7. - c. The following is a list of the 8 required font styles. For information purposes only, each font style references one or more popular fonts which embody the characteristics of the style: - (i) 0�Default (undefined) - (ii) 1�Monospaced with serifs (similar to Courier) - (iii) 2�Proportionally spaced with serifs (similar to Times New Roman) - (iv) 3�Monospaced without serifs (similar to Helvetica Monospaced) - (v) 4�Proportionally spaced without serifs (similar to Arial and Swiss) - (vi) 5�Casual font type (similar to Dom and Impress) - (vii) 6�Cursive font type (similar to Coronet and Marigold) - (viii) 7�Small capitals (similar to Engravers Gothic)

- d. Font styles may be implemented in any typeface which the decoder manufacturer deems to be a readable rendition of the font style, and need not be in the exact typefaces given in the example above. Decoders must include the ability for users to choose among the eight fonts. The decoder must display the font chosen by the caption provider unless the user chooses a different font.

**(6) Caption background color and opacity.** Captioning shall be implemented such that the caption background may be displayed in the 64 colors defined in CEA-708 and such that users are provided with the ability to override the authored color for the caption background and select from a palette of at least 8 colors including: white, black, red, green, blue, yellow, magenta, and cyan. Captioning shall be implemented such that users are provided with the ability to vary the opacity of the caption background and select between opaque, semi-transparent, and transparent background opacities. **(7) Character edge attributes.** Captioning shall be implemented such that character edge attributes may be displayed and users are provided the ability to select character edge attributes including: no edge attribute, raised edges, depressed edges, uniform edges, and drop shadowed edges. **(8) Caption window color.** Captioning shall be implemented such that the caption window color may be displayed in the 64 colors defined in CEA-708 and such that users are provided with the ability to override the authored color for the caption window and select from a palette of at least 8 colors including: white, black, red, green, blue, yellow, magenta, and cyan. Captioning shall be implemented such that users are provided with the ability to vary the opacity of the caption window and select between opaque, semi-transparent, and transparent background opacities. **(9) Language.** All players and devices must implement the ability to select between caption tracks in additional languages when such tracks are present and provide the ability for the user to select simplified or reduced captions when such captions are available and identify such a caption track as �easy reader.� **(10) Preview and setting retention.**

- a. All players and devices must provide the ability for the user to preview default and user selection of the caption features required by this section, and must retain such settings as the default caption configuration until changed by the user. - b. **As of August 17, 2026:** Video players must also provide the ability for the user to preview the appearance of closed captions while changing the caption features required by this section. The preview must be overlaid on the programming the user is currently watching. The user must be able to change the caption features and preview their appearance without exiting the video player. (Note: Stock text may be used for the caption preview.) - c. Players may leverage device-level caption settings but must also meet the preview requirements in (a) and (b) above.

**(11) Discoverability of caption controls. (as of August 17, 2026)**

- a. All user controls for adjusting caption display characteristics must be provided in one area of the settings that is accessed by an easy-to-locate and simple-to-use mechanism such as a button, key, or icon. - b. Usability testing must be conducted with consumers and disability groups to determine if the controls can be easily found, and efforts must be made to correct problems identified during that testing. (Note: Making the controls available solely or primarily through voice control does not meet this requirement.)

_Applicability:
This rule applies to help (for example, call centers, technical support, and training services) and documentation (help files, user manuals, instructions, web pages) offered by those support services for: - Devices capable of playing video programming, and - First-party video players that Microsoft preinstalls on devices or requires end-users to install on devices.

The FCC defines �video programming� as �programming provided by, or generally considered comparable to programming provided by, a television broadcast station, but not including consumer-generated media.�
